meta_title: Cut+Dry Alternative for Food Distributors in 2026
meta_desc: Keep the Cut+Dry storefront and payments, and add a reorder your accounts speak from your own guide. A Cut+Dry alternative that sits beside it instead.

hero.h1: Cut+Dry Alternative? Keep It, Let Regulars Speak Up.
hero.lead: Give your phone accounts a reorder they check themselves, and leave the platform alone. VoiceOrder Solutions goes next to Cut+Dry: your accounts say the reorder into our app from the guide you built, approve it, and send. Payments, invoicing and the storefront stay where they are.

stats.label: Freed up on each order taken off the phone
Is the go-live window for most distributors

problem.h2: What actually sends people looking for an alternative to Cut+Dry
problem.lead: Cut+Dry calls itself customer-facing ecommerce and sales enablement for foodservice, and it serves all three sides of that trade from one platform. That breadth is the product, and replacing it rarely makes sense. What sends a buyer to a Cut+Dry competitor is usually one narrower thing.

cards.h3: Some accounts would rather talk than tap
cards.body: Ordering at any hour only helps the kitchens that open the storefront. Plenty still call the office or leave a message instead, and someone at your end writes each one up.

cards.h3: Their transcription stops short of the kitchen
cards.body: The AI Order Desk turns calls and voicemail messages into orders, which is genuinely useful. Their own description mentions no step where the kitchen confirms what was transcribed, so the first person to check those lines is on your side.

cards.h3: Starting over is the expensive fix
cards.body: Cut+Dry publishes "Go Live in Under 90 Days", a good result for a platform that size. Going through a launch like that again, and moving how your customers pay, to fix one channel is out of all proportion, and no Cut+Dry alternative should ask it of you.

cards.h2: Cut+Dry for the platform, voice for the phone accounts
cards.lead: We are not a Cut+Dry replacement and could not be one. The spoken reorder adds on, so a platform already carrying your payments and your storefront is no reason to rule this out.

items.h3: Let the storefront do the storefront
items.body: Discovery, search and a published catalog are real work, and none of it happens here. The accounts who want to browse keep browsing. The ones who just want Friday's order reordered get a quicker route to it.
Our app never touches money. Nothing about adding it asks you to move how customers pay or how invoices go out, which is usually the part nobody wants to disturb.

items.h3: Our orders go where you point them
items.body: Whichever system you picked is where ours show up, over EDI, the API or QuickBooks, or by email to your desk. Nothing changes in Cut+Dry.

midcta.h3: See one spoken reorder sit beside Cut+Dry
midcta.body: Twenty minutes. One account, one order said out loud off a guide like yours, and where it lands among the orders you already get.

steps.lead: Nothing here needs a project plan, and Cut+Dry carries on as normal. You send guides, we set up accounts, your kitchens start ordering.

comparison.h2: Cut+Dry, plus VoiceOrder Solutions. One more way in.
comparison.lead: A second tool should only ever add, so the column with both never loses a row. Cut+Dry sells ecommerce, payments and sales tooling across distributors, manufacturers and restaurants, and a Cut+Dry alternative search tends to start with the accounts that use none of it. The two do not connect, and every fact about Cut+Dry comes from their own site.

faq.h2: What teams keeping Cut+Dry ask us

items.q: Does adding voice orders mean finding a Cut+Dry alternative?
items.a: No. Cut+Dry's call transcription already turns what callers say into orders, and it carries on unchanged. What VoiceOrder Solutions adds beside it is an app where the account talks through its order and approves the lines itself. The ones who browse your storefront keep browsing, and nothing gets switched off first.

items.q: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Cut+Dry?
items.a: Not at selling a catalog, collecting money, or the manufacturer side of their network. Those are what they built, and we would not ask you to give them up. Where we help is the reorder from an account you already have, spoken off your guide and approved before it sends. That narrow job is often what a Cut+Dry alternative search was really about.

items.q: Does VoiceOrder Solutions link up with Cut+Dry?
items.a: It does not. The two products have no connection, and neither vendor supports the other. Each passes its orders to your own system on its own, ours in the formats listed above. When ours come in by EDI or the API, both end up in the same system; an emailed order arrives as a file to open like any other email.

items.q: Will some kitchens be using two ordering apps?
items.a: Only the ones you offer it to. Accounts happy ordering through Cut+Dry can stay there. The app is for kitchens that still pick up the phone, which is where a spoken, checked order frees up your desk the most. Calls you keep taking get no order number from us; only what is sent through our app does.

items.q: What if a cook gets pulled away halfway through an order?
items.a: Their list stays saved where they stopped, so they can pick it up again when they are back, and nothing goes out until they send it.

items.q: How quickly can accounts start sending orders?
items.a: For most distributors this is live inside 24 to 48 hours, with a first order usually in on the same day. Nothing about your Cut+Dry setup has to change while it goes in.
Neither of us publishes a figure. Cut+Dry has a pricing page with no prices on it, and ours comes as a quote. Since that platform is staying, the thing to price is only what the voice reorder adds.

items.q: Where do the Cut+Dry details on this page come from?
items.a: All of the above was read on their own site, 10 October 2026: the module descriptions, the line about transcribing calls and the published 90 day launch. We have left their growth percentages alone, because those are their numbers. If any of it has moved on, the fault is here, not there.

mainCta.h2: Keep Cut+Dry. Add the reorder kitchens speak.
mainCta.body: Twenty minutes, one order, and one guide on the screen.
